description: Advanced Language practice, challenge and test replacement items; authored templates contextualized by day.

practice.text: Neither the director nor the assistants responsible for the science exhibition ___ prepared to revise the schedule.
options: was
were
has been
is
practice.explanation: With neither…nor, the plural nearer subject assistants requires were.

practice.text: Which sentence avoids a dangling modifier?
options: After analyzing the evidence, a discrepancy became apparent to Maya.
After analyzing the evidence, Maya noticed a discrepancy.
After analyzing the evidence, the discrepancy was noticed.
Having been analyzed, Maya noticed a discrepancy.
practice.explanation: The introductory modifier must refer to the person who analyzed the evidence.

practice.text: Which revision is most parallel? The committee valued accuracy, creativity, and ___ in the science exhibition.
options: to work efficiently
efficient work
that everyone worked efficiently
working in an efficient manner
practice.explanation: Accuracy, creativity, and efficient work are parallel noun phrases.

practice.text: Which sentence uses the correct pronoun case?
options: The scholarship was awarded to Maya and I.
Between you and I, the plan is risky.
The advisor asked Maya and me to present.
Her and Maya prepared the exhibits.
practice.explanation: Me is the object of asked; the other choices misuse a subject or object pronoun.

practice.text: By the time the judges arrived at the science exhibition, the participants ___ their presentations.
options: finish
had finished
have finished
will finish
practice.explanation: The past perfect indicates a completed action before another past event.

practice.text: Which sentence correctly joins two independent clauses?
options: The proposal was ambitious, however, it lacked evidence.
The proposal was ambitious; however, it lacked evidence.
The proposal was ambitious; however it lacked evidence.
The proposal was ambitious however; it lacked evidence.
practice.explanation: A semicolon joins the clauses, and a comma follows the conjunctive adverb however.

practice.text: Which sentence has correct subject–verb agreement?
options: Each of the entries submitted for the science exhibition have been reviewed.
The collection of essays are available online.
A number of participants is waiting outside.
The results of the latest survey have surprised the organizers.
practice.explanation: Results is plural. Each and collection are singular; a number of participants takes a plural verb.

practice.text: Which sentence is the clearest and most concise?
options: Due to the fact that the deadline was approaching, Maya worked quickly.
Because the deadline was approaching, Maya worked quickly.
The deadline being something that approached, Maya was working quickly.
In light of the fact of the deadline approaching, Maya worked quickly.
practice.explanation: Because conveys the causal connection directly without wordiness.

challenge.text: Which revision removes the ambiguous pronoun? Maya told the coordinator that the coordinator's report needed revision.
options: Maya told the coordinator that their report needed revision.
The coordinator was told by Maya that the report needed revision.
Maya told the coordinator, 'Your report needs revision.'
The report needed revision, Maya told the coordinator about it.
challenge.explanation: Your explicitly refers to the coordinator, removing the ambiguous possessive.

challenge.text: The initial findings were promising. ___, the researchers declined to announce a conclusion until the trial could be repeated.
options: Similarly
Nevertheless
For example
Consequently
challenge.explanation: Nevertheless expresses contrast between promising findings and caution.

challenge.text: Which sentence correctly expresses a hypothetical situation?
options: If Maya was the coordinator, the schedule would change.
If Maya were the coordinator, the schedule would change.
If Maya is the coordinator, the schedule would have changed.
If Maya had been the coordinator, the schedule changes.
challenge.explanation: Were is the conventional subjunctive form for a contrary-to-fact present condition.

challenge.text: Which comparison is logically complete?
options: The revised proposal was clearer than the previous committee.
The revised proposal was clearer than the previous proposal.
The revised proposal was more clearer than the previous one.
The revised proposal was clearest than the previous one.
challenge.explanation: Compare proposals with proposals, and avoid double comparative forms.

challenge.text: Which sentence correctly punctuates a restrictive clause?
options: The students, who submitted their work early, received feedback first.
The students who submitted their work early received feedback first.
The students who submitted their work early, received feedback first.
The students, who submitted their work early received feedback first.
challenge.explanation: The clause identifies which students; restrictive clauses are not enclosed in commas.

challenge.text: Which option is a complete, correctly punctuated sentence?
options: Although the committee examined every proposal.
Although the committee examined every proposal, it postponed the vote.
Examining every proposal, and then postponing the vote.
The committee examined every proposal, it postponed the vote.
challenge.explanation: The dependent although clause needs a main clause; the other options are fragments or a comma splice.

challenge.text: Which sentence correctly expresses joint ownership?
options: Maya's and the editor's shared report was published.
Maya and the editor's shared report was published.
Maya and the editors shared report was published.
Maya's and the editors' shared report was published.
challenge.explanation: For one report jointly owned by two people, place the possessive marker on the final owner.

challenge.text: Which sentence uses lie and lay correctly?
options: Yesterday Maya laid down before the science exhibition.
Yesterday Maya lay down before the science exhibition.
Yesterday Maya lain down before the science exhibition.
Yesterday Maya lays down before the science exhibition.
challenge.explanation: Lay is the simple past of intransitive lie (to recline); laid requires an object.

challenge.text: Which sentence makes clear that only the judges—not the participants—were exhausted?
options: Exhausted, the judges interviewed the participants.
The judges interviewed the exhausted participants.
The judges interviewed the participants, exhausted.
The exhausted participants were interviewed by the judges.
challenge.explanation: The adjective exhausted directly modifies judges in the introductory position.

challenge.text: Which sentence correctly uses not only…but also?
options: Maya not only revised the outline but also the bibliography.
Maya revised not only the outline but also the bibliography.
Not only Maya revised the outline but also the bibliography.
Maya not only revised the outline but the bibliography also revising.
challenge.explanation: Not only and but also must introduce grammatically parallel objects.

challenge.text: Which word best completes the sentence? The committee's decision was based on ___ evidence rather than speculation.
options: substantial
substantially
substantiate
substance
challenge.explanation: The adjective substantial modifies evidence and expresses the intended meaning.

challenge.text: Which version clearly means Maya did nothing except revise the conclusion?
options: Only Maya revised the conclusion.
Maya only revised the conclusion.
Maya revised only the conclusion.
Maya revised the only conclusion.
challenge.explanation: Only placed before revised restricts the action; revised only the conclusion restricts what was revised.

test.text: Which punctuation is correct?
options: The judges considered three criteria; accuracy, originality, and clarity.
The judges considered three criteria: accuracy, originality, and clarity.
The judges considered: three criteria, accuracy, originality, and clarity.
The judges considered three criteria, accuracy: originality, and clarity.
test.explanation: A colon can introduce a list after a complete independent clause.

test.text: Which verb completes the sentence? The quality of the submissions, not the number of participants, ___ the judges' chief concern.
options: were
have been
was
are
test.explanation: The head of the subject is singular quality, not plural submissions or participants.

test.text: Which sentence uses affect and effect correctly?
options: The revised rules will effect how the judges score.
The revised rules will affect how the judges score.
The revised rules will have an affect on scoring.
The revised rules affected an effect on scoring.
test.explanation: Affect is the verb meaning influence; effect is usually a noun meaning result.

test.text: Which opening sentence most effectively introduces an argument for extending library hours?
options: Libraries are buildings with books.
Some libraries close at six, and some close later.
Extending library hours would give students with after-school obligations more equitable access to study resources.
I am going to tell you several things about libraries.
test.explanation: The strongest thesis makes a specific, arguable claim and gives a meaningful reason.

test.text: Which sentence best supports the claim that peer review improves research?
options: Research can be difficult for many students.
Reviewers sometimes have different opinions.
Peer reviewers identified two calculation errors before the results were published.
The research topic was selected in September.
test.explanation: Concrete evidence about errors caught directly supports the claim.

test.text: Which transition best completes the argument? The first trial measured accuracy. ___, the second trial tested how consistently participants reproduced the results.
options: On the contrary
In addition
Nevertheless
As a result
test.explanation: In addition introduces a complementary second measurement rather than a contrast or consequence.

test.text: Which sentence should be removed from a paragraph explaining how to prepare for the science exhibition?
options: Participants should review the judging rubric before drafting.
A realistic rehearsal schedule helps prevent last-minute errors.
My cousin prefers strawberry ice cream to chocolate.
Practice presentations help participants identify unclear explanations.
test.explanation: The ice-cream preference is irrelevant to preparing for the event.

Some people share information, and others do not.
